home.title: A reusable foundation for PHP applications
home.lead: One website and API in a single deployment, with authentication and a Markdown Posts blog.
home.intro: sandbox_php demonstrates a small, explicit structure that is ready to adapt to your product.
home.featuresText: Visitors can read published Posts. Anyone can create an account; each signed-in user can create, edit, publish, and remove only their own Posts. Registration is available from the Login flow.
home.featureList: Server-side session registration, login, and logout.|Public blog and editor at /my-posts.|Safe Markdown preview before publishing.|JSON API and OpenAPI reference in local environments.
home.stackText: The backend uses PHP 8.4, Slim 4, PDO/MySQL, and Phinx. The interface uses Vue 3 and Vue Router as native ES modules served by Apache. There is no Node.js, npm, bundler, or JavaScript compilation step. One PHP/Apache deployment serves the site and API.
home.stackEnvironment: For development, Docker Compose provides the application and MySQL. You can also use PHP 8.4, Composer 2, the pdo_mysql and mbstring extensions, MySQL 8.4, and Apache with mod_rewrite.
home.architectureText: HTTP controllers call Application services, which use Domain entities and repository contracts. PDO implementations live in Infrastructure; Bootstrap connects dependencies and registers routes. Controllers adapt HTTP and contain no SQL. Repositories persist data without deciding business rules.
home.architecturePaths: src/Domain/User and src/Domain/Post: rules, invariants, and contracts.|src/Application: application operations without Slim or PDO.|src/Infrastructure: controllers, sessions, Markdown, and MySQL repositories.|src/Bootstrap: configuration, composition, and routes.|public/assets: Vue modules, CSS, and local libraries.|database/migrations and tests: versioned schema and checks.
home.architectureExtension: To add a domain, create its contracts and implementations in their respective layers and connect them in Bootstrap.
home.installText: With Docker Engine and Docker Compose v2 installed, clone the repository, configure local credentials, and start the services. The application is available at http://localhost:8080. Migrations do not run automatically; apply them explicitly.
home.installMigration: The initial migration is applied explicitly; check its status after running it.
home.installEnvironment: Use .env only for local settings, keep it out of version control, and replace every example password.
home.auth: Registration, login, and the Posts workflow
home.authList: Open Login and follow the registration link to create an account.|Sign in; the menu shows My Posts and Log out.|In My Posts, create a draft with a title and Markdown.|Review the preview, save, and publish. The published Post appears in the Blog.|Edit, unpublish, or delete only Posts owned by your account.
home.authSecurity: Passwords are stored as hashes. The session is regenerated at login, authenticated mutations require CSRF, and the backend checks ownership for each operation. This demo has no password recovery or attempt limit; define recovery and abuse controls before exposing a derived application publicly.
home.routesText: Unknown /api/* routes return JSON 404 responses. Unknown page paths show the not-found screen. The /docs route serves Swagger UI and OpenAPI when enabled in configuration.
home.routesList: /: introduction and documentation.|/blog and /blog/{slug}: public reading of published Posts.|/login and /register: authentication.|/my-posts: editor for the signed-in user's Posts.|/api/auth/*, /api/posts*, and /api/me/posts*: session, reading, and editing API.|/docs: Swagger UI and OpenAPI when enabled.
home.qualityText: Run Composer commands in the app container. With Chrome or Chromium on the host, also check the browser and Vue modules with ./tools/test-frontend.sh. The composer quality gate includes lint, PHPUnit with minimum coverage, PHPStan, and the OpenAPI check.
home.qualityCommands: Run formatting, lint, tests, and the full quality gate with the commands below.
home.qualityDetails: composer quality checks lint, PHPUnit with minimum coverage, PHPStan, and OpenAPI. composer format changes files; the other commands only check them.
home.securityText: Use compose.prod.yaml and an environment file outside the repository. Set your own secrets, APP_ENV=production, APP_DEBUG=false, OPENAPI_ENABLED=false, and a public HTTPS APP_URL. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy and do not expose MySQL to the internet. Back up the database before upgrades and apply migrations as a controlled step.
home.securityCookie: The session cookie receives Secure when the public URL uses HTTPS. Keep environment files and database backups outside the public directory. Registration is open, and this demo has no password recovery or rate limiting; assess and implement those controls before publishing a derived application.
home.securityVue: Vue templates are compiled by the browser runtime. Do not accept user-provided Vue templates or executable HTML. Markdown preview escapes raw HTML and blocks unsafe links.
home.customizationText: Adapt User fields and Auth flows to the derived product. Preserve password hashing, secure sessions, login session regeneration, CSRF, and backend authorization. Keep rules in Domain, orchestration in Application, and integrations in Infrastructure; connect dependencies and routes in Bootstrap.
home.customizationModel: When changing the data model, update the entity, repository contract, PDO implementation, migration, API, and tests together.
home.customizationDomain: For a new domain, keep rules in Domain, orchestration in Application, and integrations in Infrastructure. Register dependencies and routes in Bootstrap. Prefer focused contracts over generic extension abstractions; current source and tests contain examples.
home.sddText: The standalone SDD Lite skill provides a shared workflow for defining, planning, implementing, and reviewing changes. Project-specific context and implementation conventions are recorded in this repository.
home.sddDetails: Feature records use feature.md, spec.md, plan.md, and review.md. Historical records may retain their original format.
home.sddStart: Invoke $sdd-lite with a command such as feature, spec, plan, code, or review. Read the skill instructions for its usage.
